questions.q: In SOQL, how are literal date values written in a WHERE clause?
options: In double quotes, e.g. WHERE CloseDate = "2026-01-15"
In single quotes, e.g. WHERE CloseDate = '2026-01-15'
Without quotes, e.g. WHERE CloseDate = 2026-01-15
Wrapped in a DATE() function always
questions.explain: Unlike strings, SOQL date literals are written bare, without surrounding quotes.

questions.q: What does a date literal like LAST_N_DAYS:30 represent?
options: A function that only works inside aggregate queries
A single fixed calendar date that must be updated manually over time
A field name alias for CreatedDate
A relative span of time, evaluated fresh every time the query runs
questions.explain: Date literals are relative expressions re-evaluated against the current day every time the query runs, avoiding the need to hardcode and maintain fixed dates.

questions.q: What does WHERE CreatedDate = THIS_MONTH return?
options: Every record created at any point during the current month
Only records created exactly today
A syntax error, because = cannot be used with a calendar-period literal
Only records created on the first day of the month
questions.explain: Because a calendar-period literal represents a whole span of time, = with that literal means 'falls within this range', not 'exactly equal to one instant'.

questions.q: To find records from the end of last quarter onward (not records within last quarter itself), which operator should you use with LAST_QUARTER?
options: = (equals)
> (greater than)
LIKE
IN
questions.explain: Using > filters to one side of the literal's boundary — everything after last quarter ended — rather than matching the span itself.

questions.q: What is a practical reason a report might look 'off by a day' around month boundaries when filtering a datetime field?
options: GROUP BY must be used with any datetime filter
SOQL date literals are always off by exactly 24 hours
A time zone artifact, since datetime comparisons relate to GMT internally but are reasoned about in the running user's time zone
Datetime fields cannot be filtered with date literals at all
questions.explain: Time zone differences between GMT-based internal storage and the user's local time zone are a common, non-bug cause of apparent off-by-a-day discrepancies at date boundaries.
